newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen flat until year-end.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen flat until year-end.

text.p: Polish shares eased in lower turnover on Monday after a three-day rise and analysts said the market could stay in its already six-week long horizontal trend in light trade for the rest of the month.

"It seems the end of the year does not abet the making of strategic decisions by large investors...who haven't yet formed their strategies for next year," said Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.
Analysts said the slightly stronger buying after price fixing could signal a slight gain on Tuesday but that the market could stay between 13,600 and 14,000 points this week.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.3 percent to 13,667.0 and turnover fell 17.4 percent to 75.2 million zlotys ($26.3 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 35 to 31 with 17 stocks flat.

Some analysts said gains toward 15,000 points could begin early next year, as there were no new primary market offerings on the immediate horizon and December earnings reports, most due on Wednesday, could continue the second half's slight earnings uptrend.
Analysts said Monday's news year-on-year inflation fell to 19.1 percent in November would not significantly affect shares.
Year-on-year inflation was at 19.5 percent in October, and analysts said the November figure was no surprise, while the central bank has said no interest rate cut was forthcoming.
Analysts said top gainers, construction firm Mostostal Zabrze and meat processor Sokolow, up 5.6 and 4.4 percent in active trade, might have seen speculative gains before releasing earnings.
Continuous trade turnover was at 3.1 million zlotys ($1.1) with five stocks up and six flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 3.8 percent to 138.5 zlotys ($48.4) and rose 1.1 percent to 139.5 zlotys ($48.8) in 8.5-million-zloty live trade.
